text: The International Prize in Statistics is awarded every two years to an individual or team for major achievements using statistics to advance science, technology, and human welfare. Alongside the COPSS Presidents' Award, it is considered the two highest honours in the field of statistics. Modeled after the Nobel Prizes, Abel Prize, Fields Medal, and Turing Award, the prize includes a monetary award of $80,000 and is presented during the World Statistics Congress. It recognizes a single work or body of work that embodies a powerful and original idea with significant impact across other disciplines or practical benefits to the world. The recipient must be alive at the time of the award. The prize is administered by the International Prize in Statistics Foundation, which includes representatives from major learned societies. In addition to honoring statisticians, the Foundation seeks to educate the public about statistical innovations and increase the field's visibility. The recipient is selected by an international committee of experts in statistics. As of 2016, the committee members were Xiao-Li Meng (Harvard University), Sally Morton (Virginia Tech), Stephen Senn (Luxembourg Institute of Health), Bernard Silverman (University of Oxford), Stephen Stigler (University of Chicago), Susan Wilson (Australian National University), and Bin Yu (University of California, Berkeley). As of May 2022, the selection committee members are Yoav Benjamini, Francisco Cribari-Neto, Vijay Nair, Sonia Petrone, Nancy Reid, Sylvia Richardson, and Jane-Ling Wang.
